Assessment & Plan (Integrating DDx)

Key findings: 32-year-old male with 6-week intermittent unilateral (left) hearing loss, tinnitus, mild disequilibrium. No pain, otorrhoea, fever, or systemic symptoms.  

Differential diagnoses (consistent with transcript):  
• Cerumen impaction – most likely, common reversible conductive loss; otoscopy required.  
• Menière’s disease – possible given fluctuating loss + tinnitus + imbalance, though vertigo not classic.  
• Serous otitis media/Eustachian-tube dysfunction – possible middle-ear effusion causing conductive loss.  

Working impression: Unilateral conductive hearing loss—rule out cerumen impaction first.  

Management Plan

• Arrange face-to-face GP appointment within 4–5 days for otoscopic examination to assess for wax, middle-ear effusion, or other pathology.  
• Provide patient with educational leaflet on tinnitus (link placed in notes).  
• Advise patient to phone support team to book appointment; contact service earlier if symptoms worsen.  
• Follow-up: review findings after otoscopy and determine need for audiometry, ENT referral, or further imaging depending on results.

- Allied health referral (EPC – 10 visits):  Not recorded.  
- Reproductive or sexual health clinic referral:  Not recorded.  
- Mental health support if indicated (e.g., psychologist, AMS support):  Not recorded.  
- CTG registration:  Not recorded.  
- Preventive health follow-up booked (e.g., flu vaccine, Pap test):  Not recorded.  

Summary of Differential Diagnoses (from DDx):

1. Cerumen impaction – High likelihood: gradual unilateral muffled hearing, tinnitus, easily confirmed/excluded by otoscopy.  
2. Menière’s disease – Moderate likelihood: unilateral fluctuating loss + tinnitus + imbalance, though vertigo not classic and duration continuous.  
3. Serous otitis media/Eustachian-tube dysfunction – Moderate likelihood: conductive loss over weeks without pain or fever; needs otoscopy to confirm.
